name: U.S. Federation of Worker Cooperatives
description: The national membership organization for worker cooperatives in the US, advancing worker-owned and worker-governed workplaces through education, technical assistance, and advocacy. Founded in 2004 out of a national gathering of regional worker-co-op practitioners. Represents nearly 450 business and organizational members, standing in for an estimated 1,300 US worker co-ops and roughly 15,000 workers. Governed by a 100% member-elected board; offices in Oakland, CA and Philadelphia, PA. Co-hosts the annual Worker Co-op Conference with the Democracy at Work Institute.

notRepresentable: USFWC's peer network and council meetings (Cannabis, Media, Black Cooperator, Union Co-ops, Racial & Economic Justice, and the Spanish-language Immigrant Movement council) recur monthly, which a single event date cannot express. They are also oriented to existing members rather than newcomers.
research.notes: USFWC's records predate content/RESEARCH.md, so this is its first documented pass rather than new discovery. It found two things the seed content had missed: the Spanish-language WhatsApp group listed alongside the Slack on the same Connect page, and the Worker Cooperative Startup Webinar — the one entry on a ten-item calendar explicitly open to anyone rather than to members.
